record.context_brief: Maximal finite subgroups of Euclidean isometry groups
record.original_question: Let Γ act effectively, isometrically, and totally discontinuously on Euclidean space E^n. Prove that, up to conjugation in Γ, there are at most 2^n maximal finite subgroups of Γ.

evidence.quote: Suppose that a group Γ acts effectively, isometrically, and totally discontinuously on Euclidean space E^n. Show that Γ contains at most 2^n maximal finite subgroups up to conjugation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E^n$ denote $n$-dimensional Euclidean space, and let $\mathrm{Isom}(E^n)$ be its group of isometries. Suppose $\Gamma \le \mathrm{Isom}(E^n)$ acts on $E^n$ effectively, isometrically, and properly discontinuously (totally discontinuously), meaning that the action homomorphism is injective and that for every compact set $K \subseteq E^n$ the set $\{\gamma \in \Gamma : \gamma K \cap K \neq \emptyset\}$ is finite. A subgroup $F \le \Gamma$ is called a maximal finite subgroup if $F$ is finite and is not properly contained in any finite subgroup of $\Gamma$. Two subgroups $F_1, F_2 \le \Gamma$ are conjugate in $\Gamma$ if there exists $\gamma \in \Gamma$ with $\gamma F_1 \gamma^{-1} = F_2$.

Prove that the number of conjugacy classes (in $\Gamma$) of maximal finite subgroups of $\Gamma$ is at most $2^n$.
artifact.status_search_result: A direct web search did not return a definitive source confirming or refuting the bound of $2^n$ conjugacy classes of maximal finite subgroups in an $n$-dimensional crystallographic-type group. Standard references on crystallographic groups (Bieberbach, Plesken–Pohst classifications) study maximal finite subgroups of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z})$ and stabilizers in space groups, but no clearly authoritative statement of this exact bound was located, so the status is recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Crystallographic group - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: General background on crystallographic groups and their finite point groups.
status_evidence.claim: Provides standard framework for finite subgroups of Euclidean isometry groups but does not state the 2^n bound.

status_evidence.title: Finite subgroups of the group GL(n,Z)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of finite subgroups of GL(n,Z) and maximal irreducible finite subgroups.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature on maximal finite subgroups; does not directly address the conjugacy-class count 2^n in Γ.
